title: Small-context microbenchmark matrix + adoption signals for short-sequence LLMs
creator: Leah Moreno
description:
Goal: Produce a defensible, repeatable microbenchmark and market signal pack focused on short-context LLM behavior (approx. 50–512 tokens) to inform product routing, latency SLAs, and a model substitution cost estimator for enterprise RAG flows.

Scope and deliverables:
- Microbenchmark matrix (quantized and fp16) across candidate open models and Redwood-verified variants measuring: first-token latency, median token latency, p95/p99/p999 tail latencies, KV cache rehydrate time, and token-throughput under continuous batching for short sequences.
- Adoption signals dataset combining public model release velocity, community-run latency/accuracy reports, and customer feedback telemetry (anonymized) to estimate enterprise readiness and migration risk.
- Substitution cost estimator: per-100k-query cost delta for swapping model families under short-context workloads, factoring in quantization impact and dedicated vs hosted pricing.
- Recommendation deck (internal) with routing rules (latency-first, cost-fallback), and a skeleton alerting policy for Console to flag when a model's short-context tail latency regresses beyond threshold.

Approach and trade-offs:
- Focus on short-context because many RAG and chat entrypoints are dominated by sub-512 token flows where first-token and tail latency are disproportionately important for UX.
- We will prioritize a reproducible harness (colab + GH Actions) for continuous benchmarking over a one-off lab run; that increases engineering effort but gives continuous signals.
- Accuracy benchmarks will be lightweight (prompt set / micro-eval) to avoid conflating latency signals with large-scale capability evals; follow-up epic will expand capability regressions if any substitution triggers high customer impact.

Success criteria:
- Deliver microbench matrix with at least 6 model variants (open-source and Redwood-verified) and baseline numbers for first-token, p95, p99, and throughput under 1s median first-token.
- A working substitution-cost prototype that produces per-workload delta estimates within 20% of observed billing for two pilot customers.
- Routing policy recommendations accepted by Runtime and Console PMs and merged into the routing RFC repo.

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- Large-context (>2048 tokens) benchmarking, which will be handled in a separate initiative.
- Full scale accuracy regression lab and drift detection dashboards (follow-up).

Stakeholders and reviewers:
- Runtime engineering (for harness and kernel-selection insights)
- Observability/Console (for alert wiring and dashboard visuals)
- Solutions & Sales (for customer pilot instrumentation)

Notes on data and privacy:
- Customer telemetry will be sampled and anonymized; we will work with Security to confirm no PII leaves the corp VPC.

Next steps:
1) Align with Runtime on harness repo and runner infra (due 2026-02-26).
2) Finalize model candidate list and quantization matrices (due 2026-03-02).
3) Kick off 2-week pilot run and ship initial deck (due 2026-03-12).
